::: notes
Welcome. We have a full day in four parts, all of it on one published experiment, in which just over a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing. The first part sets up the rest: what we do when we do social science, why many researchers think that it is in crisis, and the three large studies of SCORE that measured how often published findings survive being repeated. The second asks which question the claim of the paper actually answers, and in the third you reproduce one of the five independent reanalyses of that claim, the one that I give you. Most of the work comes in the fourth part, where you vary the analysis yourself, we read the class chart against every justifiable analysis of these data, and you preregister the one analysis that you would publish and run it again on the data of the new experiment that tested the claim.
:::
